title: Timeline: The Path to Arbitrary Prosecution
subtitle: From a transparent commercial process to cross-border repression.
intro: This chronicle is documentary evidence of how legal institutions are used to create a veneer of legality where none exists. The sequence of events reveals the intent of the investigation: a man living openly and working legally learned of his status as a 'criminal' only at the moment of his arrest in another country.

events.title: Independent Consultant: A Decade of Exemplary Service
events.text: Dmitry Lagovsky worked with FEZ JSC as an outside legal consultant (sole practitioner). He was not an officer of the enterprise. In over 10 years of cooperation, not a single complaint was ever raised against his work, either by the plant or by regulators.

events.title: Corporate Conflict: Attempted Takeover
events.text: Minority shareholder S.V. Palkin initiated a series of attacks on the plant's management. Lagovsky, acting strictly within the law, provided legal defense for the enterprise. In December 2021, the plant completed a land sale — an act that would later be artificially criminalised.

events.title: Opening of the Case: Procedural Fabrication
events.text: Investigator Salikov Yu.M. opened a criminal case under Part 4, Art. 159 of the RF Criminal Code. The violation is fundamental: the case was opened without a complaint from the plant itself (the alleged 'victim'). Lagovsky was questioned as a witness, faced no claims, and was not restricted in his movements.

events.title: Legal Relocation to Serbia
events.text: Lagovsky's family moved to Belgrade. The relocation was entirely legal: valid passports, residence permits, official employment. Lagovsky was not in hiding — his address in Serbia was available to the authorities. The reason for departure was his anti-war stance and the risk of forced mobilisation.

events.title: Secret Indictment: Denial of the Right to Defense
events.text: A year and a half after the case was opened, investigators secretly issued a resolution charging Lagovsky as a defendant. He was not notified, despite his address being known. In June 2024, the RF state system (Gosuslugi) officially confirmed to Lagovsky: no criminal prosecution existed. This is documented state-level disinformation.

events.title: Arbitration Triumph: Transaction Ruled Lawful
events.text: The Arbitration Court ruled: the land sale was legal and beneficial for the plant. This decision was upheld by all instances, including the RF Supreme Court. From this moment, the criminal case lost all legal meaning, yet the prosecution only intensified.

events.title: In-absentia Arrest: Finalising the Arbitrariness
events.text: The Tversky Court of Moscow issued an in-absentia arrest warrant. Lagovsky was placed on an international wanted list as 'absconding,' though he had never received a summons and lived at an officially registered address in Belgrade.

events.title: Arrest in Belgrade: The Moment of Truth
events.text: Lagovsky was detained by Serbian police. Only at this moment — two and a half years after the case began — did he learn he was a 'wanted criminal.' The extradition process commenced.

events.title: Serbian Court: Denial of Justice
events.text: The Higher and Appellate Courts of Belgrade approved extradition. The courts demonstratively refused to consider the RF arbitration rulings confirming Lagovsky's innocence, stating their role was a 'technical document check.'

events.title: Asylum Refusal: Ignoring Reality
events.text: The Serbian Asylum Office and Commission rejected the asylum request. Authorities acknowledged the mobilisation risk but refused to classify it as a ground for protection, ignoring Articles 3 and 8 ECHR.

events.title: Administrative Court: The Final Domestic Barrier
events.text: The case has been referred to the Serbian Administrative Court. This is the last chance for the Serbian justice system to prove its independence and commitment to European human rights standards.

summary: The timeline of the case proves that the prosecution of Dmitry Lagovsky is artificial and repressive. The secret indictment while his address was known, the disregard for exculpatory RF Supreme Court acts, and the formalistic approach of Serbian courts form a clear picture of a 'flagrant denial of justice'.
